text:
alex: Hi all — first week here! Quick q: I'm building a small embeddings pipeline for a demo. Should I use my hosted API key or the sandbox key? Trying to understand quota/rate limits for batch embeddings vs generation. Also, any recommended batch size? TIA

maria-devex: welcome! :tada: For local dev & demos use the sandbox key. Hosted keys are for prod and billing. Sandbox has limited quota but is fine for demos. Also note sandbox blocks streaming and has stricter per-minute units. See internal devex doc: https://redwood.internal/devex/keys

alex: thanks — any numbers on per-minute or per-request limits for embeddings in sandbox? I'm planning to send batches of ~500 short docs (each ~100 tokens).

sam-infra: sandbox has a soft per-minute unit cap and per-request practical limit. For embeddings we usually cap requests around 1000 vectors per request on hosted, but sandbox avoids >500 to keep the pool healthy. If you plan 500, split into ~200-250 per request to reduce 429 risk.

jenna-eng: also watch concurrent request limits for your account. Hosted/Dedicated can handle higher qps (especially Dedicated), but hosted accounts are rate-limited per-key. For embeddings cost/units differ by model — embed-1b is cheaper than embed-4b.

maria-devex: quick rules of thumb: batch size 128–256 is a sweet spot balancing latency and throughput on hosted. For embeddings use the non-streaming endpoint POST /v1/embeddings. Example curl: 

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings
 -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_SANDBOX_KEY"
 -H "Content-Type: application/json"
 -d '{"model":"embed-1b","input":["doc1","doc2",...]}'
```

alex: solid. If I hit 429s locally, should I exponential backoff? Any recommended retry headers to watch for?

sam-infra: yes — on 429 do exponential backoff with jitter. Check for a Retry-After header; if present, respect it. If you see repeated 429s, try halving the batch size after 2–3 retries. Also include idempotency where possible so you can safely retry.

onboarding-bot: Tip: to request a temporary sandbox bump, ping @maria-devex with the time window and expected units and she can file the request.

alex: one more: I need embeddings for ~20k docs for a proof-of-concept — should I request a one-off quota bump or use hosted trial credits?

maria-devex: for 20k short docs, request a one-off bump (please include dataset size, model you plan to use, and expected QPS). Hosted trial credits are fine for short evaluations but they can expire and may be throttled; if you need stable throughput for a demo we can provision an ephemeral hosted/demo key instead.

jenna-eng: fyi: for large batches consider offline preprocessing, caching, and incremental indexing so you don't re-embed repeatedly. Also consider compressing inputs or deduplicating near-duplicates before calling the API.

alex: thanks all — I'll split to ~200-per request, add exponential backoff with jitter, and ping maria for a bump if needed. Really appreciate the quick responses :smile:

maria-devex: lmk and I can submit the bump request for you now.

alex: will do, thanks :thumbsup:
